The Illusion

The 2M Token Illusion

Context Capacity Does Not Equal Focused Reasoning

The Marketing Promise

  • "Drop your entire repo" — No need to curate or filter files.
  • Infinite memory — Treat the prompt as an external hard drive.
  • Zero effort — The model will figure out what matters.

The Production Reality

  • Zombie Code Priming — Model repeats obsolete patterns it just read.
  • Constraint Bleed — Critical architectural boundaries get diluted.
  • Multi-Hop Collapse — Connections across 100k+ tokens break down.
"Context capacity measures how much data can fit in RAM. Context engineering measures whether the model actually attends to what matters."
Conference Keynote Context capacity is a storage metric, not a focus metric 2 / 12
The Math

The Softmax Attention Equation

The Mathematical Physics of the Attention Mechanism
\[\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V\]
Query (Q)
CURRENT TOKEN

The token currently being generated by the model right now.

Key (K)
PRIOR TOKENS

Semantic index addresses of every prior token in your prompt history.

Value (V)
INFORMATION PAYLOAD

The actual information content retrieved and projected forward.

Conference Keynote Scaled Dot-Product Attention: Vaswani et al., 2017 3 / 12
The Math

The Zero-Sum Attention Budget

Why Every Additional Token Dilutes Critical Rules
\[a_{ij} = \frac{\exp(s_{ij})}{\sum_{m=1}^{N} \exp(s_{im})}\]
\[\sum_{j=1}^{N} a_{ij} = 1.0 \quad (100\%)\]

The 100-Point Budget Rule

  • Attention is a zero-sum game: Total weight is exactly 100 points.
  • 50-token prompt: 3 critical rules share ~30 points each. Laser focus.
  • 50,000-token prompt: Same rules receive ~0.05 points each. Crushed by noise.
"You cannot increase the attention numerator without swelling the denominator. Every irrelevant line of code steals focus from your core requirement."
Conference Keynote Sum of attention weights is always identically 1.0 (100%) 4 / 12
Context Rot

The Three Pathologies of Context Rot

How Attention Dilution Breaks Real Code in Real Projects
1. Zombie Code
NEGATIVE PRIMING

The model treats obsolete, broken code in early chat turns as the primary template for new generation.

2. Constraint Bleed
SOFTMAX DILUTION

Rules established in prompt #1 ("Never use Any", "Always write unit tests") fade out after 20 chat messages.

3. Multi-Hop Collapse
REASONING BREAKDOWN

Connecting 3+ architectural dependencies across 100k tokens becomes mathematically intractable.

"Context Rot is not a bug in the model weights—it is an inevitable consequence of prompt entropy over time."
Conference Keynote Diagnosing LLM performance collapse in prolonged sessions 5 / 12
Mental Models

The Kitchen Order Analogy

Why Your IDE Chat Is Like an Overcrowded Restaurant Kitchen

The 3-Ticket Order Board

  • Ticket 1: Burger, medium rare.
  • Ticket 2: Severe Peanut Allergy!
  • Chef's Attention: 95% on the allergy warning.
  • Outcome: Flawless, safe execution.

The 200-Ticket Avalanche

  • Desk covered: Yesterday's receipts, coffee stains, 80 old orders.
  • Same Allergy Warning: Buried on ticket #42 under receipts.
  • Chef's Attention: 0.5% on allergy rule.
  • Outcome: Emergency room.
"Your AI assistant is that chef. Every long chat with 50 failed attempts is yesterday's receipts cluttering the counter."

The Math

Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE)

The 'Lost in the Middle' Phenomenon Is Built Into Math

The Attention Distribution Curve

  • Primacy Effect (Start): System prompts and instructions receive high initial attention.
  • Recency Effect (End): The latest user prompt receives high immediate attention.
  • The Middle Valley (Trough): Tokens placed between 20% and 80% of context suffer severe attention decay.
U-Curve
Attention Distribution Profile
▲ START: System Prompt (High Attention)
▼ MIDDLE: The Dead Zone (Attenuated)
▲ END: Current Query (High Attention)
"Never put critical architectural constraints in the middle of a 100k-token prompt. If it must be followed, place it at the root or right before generation."
Conference Keynote Liu et al. (2023) - Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts 7 / 12
Solutions

Attention Budgeting in Practice

Architecting Context Like You Architect Memory Hierarchy
Level 1: Global
REPO LEVEL (L0)

Universal facts only: Java 21, Spring Boot 3.4, no Lombok, tabs vs spaces.

Target: < 50 lines
Level 2: Scoped
DIRECTORY LEVEL (L1)

Triggered only on matching files via applyTo: "frontend/" or applyTo: "*.sql".

Zero token cost until invoked
Level 3: Inline
TASK LEVEL (L2)

Precise task context: #file:orderService.ts + acceptance criteria for the current turn.

Discarded on task completion
"Document the unique, not the universal. If an LLM already knows it from its pretraining, do NOT put it in your system instructions."
Conference Keynote Context Engineering Tier: Global -> Scoped -> Dynamic Inline 8 / 12
Solutions

Scoped Context via applyTo Globs

Loading Rules on Demand to Preserve Attention Mass

The Fat Prompt Anti-Pattern

# Mega Prompt (Loaded Everywhere)
- React conventions... (40 lines)
- PostgreSQL rules... (50 lines)
- Spring Boot architecture... (60 lines)
- Kubernetes YAML syntax... (30 lines)

Total: 180 lines in EVERY prompt!
Attention wasted: ~80%

The Scoped Pattern

---
applyTo: "frontend/src//*.ts"
---

Angular Rules

- Always use OnPush change detection
- Use signals for reactive local state
- Freya design system components only

Total: 15 lines (loaded only when needed!)
"By scoping rules to file globs, the LLM receives maximum attention density on the relevant technology stack."
Conference Keynote VS Code Scoped Instructions Pattern: .github/instructions/*.instructions.md 9 / 12

Matching Context Size and Reasoning Effort to the Real Task

Context Size Reasoning Effort Ideal Workload Production Verdict
Minimal (<16k) High (Reasoning) Complex refactoring, concurrency bugs, TDD loops, security review ★ SWEET SPOT: Zero rot, surgical precision
Massive (1M+) Low (Scan) Repository audits, API drift detection, legacy codebase mapping ★ SWEET SPOT: Broad synthesis, fast scan

"Golden Engineering Law: If you need deep reasoning, make context small. If you need wide context, keep reasoning shallow."

Takeaways

The 5 Golden Rules of Context Engineering

What You Should Do Tomorrow Morning at Your Desk
  • 1. The 15-Message Rule: When a task is complete or goes off track, start a fresh chat (Ctrl+L). Don't argue with zombie code.
  • 2. Document the Unique: Only put things in instructions that the model cannot know from pretraining.
  • 3. Scope Everything: Use applyTo globs instead of giant monolithic instruction files.
  • 4. Mind the U-Curve: Put mission-critical constraints at the very top or in the final prompt, never in the middle.
  • 5. Stay on the Diagonal: High reasoning demands tiny context. Broad context demands shallow tasks.
"Context is a scarce attention budget, not a garbage bin. Engineer it with the same discipline you engineer your database queries."
Conference Keynote Practical heuristics for daily AI-assisted software engineering 11 / 12
